messages.subject_clean: [Bioc-devel] Request to rename devel-only package BamScale to BamScaleR before the 3.24 release
messages.body_plain:
Wanted to follow up on this and the recommendation to submit to the new
submission queue?

On Fri, Sep 4, 2026 at 7:17?AM Kern, Lori <Lori.Shepherd at roswellpark.org>
wrote:

> Thank you for your inquiry.
>
> I agree there is no need to deprecate and we can handle the renaming.
>
> I would however recommend still submitting onto BiocContributions as the
> renamed package including all internal references and having it added via
> the automatic process to make sure everything is changed on our system
> completely.   Since they are different names we can then wait until its on
> the system to remove the old version in devel.   Once submitted and
> policies accepted, please tag me (@lshep) and I will handle the expediated
> process and make sure it stays on my queue to remove the old.
>
> Thank you
>
>
>
> Lori Kern
>
> Bioconductor Core Team
>
> Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center
>
> Department of Biostatistics & Bioinformatics
>
> Elm & Carlton Streets
>
> Buffalo, New York 14263

> *From:* Bioc-devel <bioc-devel-bounces at r-project.org> on behalf of Chirag
> Parsania <chirag.parsania at gmail.com>
> *Sent:* Thursday, September 3, 2026 10:52 PM
> *To:* maintainer at bioconductor.org <maintainer at bioconductor.org>
> *Cc:* bioc-devel at r-project.org <bioc-devel at r-project.org>
> *Subject:* [Bioc-devel] Request to rename devel-only package BamScale to
> BamScaleR before the 3.24 release
>
> Dear Bioconductor core team,
>
> I maintain BamScale, which was accepted on 4 May 2026
> (Bioconductor/Contributions issue #4128) and is currently in the 3.24 devel
> nightly builds at version 0.99.14. The package has never been part of a
> Bioconductor release.
>
> I would like to rename it to BamScaleR before the 3.24 release. The reason
> is [REASON, e.g. to avoid confusion with the existing BAMscale command-line
> tool from NCBI (github.com/ncbi/BAMscale), which does something
> different]. I have checked that BamScaleR does not exist on CRAN or in
> Bioconductor (BiocManager::install("BamScaleR") fails and the name is
> absent from the 3.24 manifest).
>
> I am aware that the guidelines describe renaming as deprecating the old
> package and resubmitting the new one for review. Since BamScale has not
> been in any release, there are no users to protect with a deprecation
> cycle. I noticed the same situation was handled by renaming the repository
> directly for SingleRBookWrapper -> SingleRBook (Contributions #1609) and
> scTypeR -> scClassifR (Contributions #1798), and I hope the same is
> possible here.
>
> Concretely, could you:
>
>   1. rename packages/BamScale to packages/BamScaleR on
> git.bioconductor.org,
>   2. update the entry in the 3.24 software manifest,
>   3. update the push-access configuration so my SSH key maps to the new
> repository,
>   4. let me know whether I should push the renamed DESCRIPTION before or
> after
>      your change.
>
> On my side I will rename the GitHub repository (cparsania/BamScale ->
> cparsania/BamScaleR), change the Package field and all internal references
> (useDynLib, native routine registration, vignette, documentation, URLs),
> bump to  0.99.15, and push to the renamed upstream to trigger a build. The
> version will stay in the 0.99.x pre-release series.
>
> I would like to complete this well before the release branch for 3.24 is
> created, so the renamed package gets clean nightly builds first. If you
> would rather I go through the deprecate-and-resubmit route via
> BiocContributions instead, I will do that, though I would hope to avoid
> missing the 3.24 release.
>
> Thank you very much for your help.
>
> Best regards,
> Dr. Chirag Parsania
> Maintainer, BamScale
>

messages.subject_clean: [Bioc-devel] Package home pages with >1 URL have broken links
messages.body_plain:
The example on page 4 of the "Writing R Extensions" manual shows that the URL field fo the DESCRIPTION file can contain a list of comma-separated URLs.

Until very recently, the two URLs given in edgeR's DESCRIPTION file were rendered correctly on the edgeR home page. After the most recent website revision, though, the two URLs are now pasted together into one href URL, which of course fails if a users clicks on it.
https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/bioc/html/edgeR.html

PS. I did much prefer the old home pages! A lot of features that I found useful have now been removed.

Regards
Gordon

---------------------------------------
Professor Gordon K Smyth
Lab Head, Tech Sciences Division, WEHI
htttps://gksmyth.github.io

messages.subject: [Bioc-devel] Waiting for new package revision.
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

(I'm not sure this is the best place to write. Please let me know if there's somewhere else I'd should go.)

I submitted a package on June to the old submission system which I the resubmitted on June 22nd?to the new system, everything built clean at first attempt and a reviewer was assigned on the same day. Since then I received a message from the reviewer on July 29th telling me that the package was on his queue but had two other ones before. Since then I've not received any other message and nobody has answered my questions and requests for an updated expected time for the revision. I know the reviewers are volunteers and that time might not be available for reviews, but it's been three and a half months since submission and I'm starting to think that it might not be included in the next release.

Any idea on how to proceed??

The issue for the package is: https://github.com/Bioconductor/BiocContributions/issues/68

Thanks a lot

Bernat

messages.body_plain:
Dear Bioconductor community,

I am sharing a perspective article proposing a wearable EEG framework ? the
Psychiatric State Index (PSI) ? for real-time differentiation of autistic
meltdowns from psychotic episodes using EEG-derived biomarkers and machine
learning.

The computational framework uses personal baseline z-score normalization
across 10 EEG sub-components, a two-stage classification pipeline (on-chip
SVM + cloud LSTM/Transformer), and may be of interest to those developing
EEG signal processing and biomarker analysis pipelines.

Full article (PDF) available upon request.

Netanel Stern
Independent Security Researcher and Clinical AI Developer
Rosh HaAyin, Israel

Hi Sean,

Thanks for making updates. Looking at the limma home page, some things that still look odd include:

- The badge and the Details give different estimates of how long the package has been in Bioconductor (and why give the same info twice anyway).
- The badge and the Detail repeat downloads rank, which is unnecessary duplication. The later takes quite of bit of vertical space to give the same info, so it would be one that I would remove.
- Under Documentation, the text "A brief introduction to limma", "limma User's Guide", "Reference Manual", and "NEWS" all have live links, but the links are degenerate because they just lead back to the same page.
- Could the link for NEWS be HTML instead of Text?
- Installation instructions are given twice, once under Installation and once under "Downloads".
- Under Imports and Suggests, most package names come with live links, but the base packages do not. The 'splines' package is not part of the default R installation, so I wonder why it doesn't have a live link? Not that this is terribly important.
- There's still no link to the code Browser, but I don't mind that. The git commands to access the source repository are far more important IMO.
- There is in general much too much vertical white space on the page for my taste. I guess that's the current modern style to allow for thick thumbs and smart phone access, but to this old dinosaur the page looks rather sparse even on my iphone.

BTW, it would be interesting to know some background information on why the home pages are completely redone like this. They seemed ok as they were, so I assume that it must have something to do with rebuilding the backend. What's happening? It would be interesting to know what the plans are.

Regards
Gordon

messages.body_plain:
Thanks, again, Gordon, for the comments and entirely warranted questions about the background for the changes.

The package pages weren't redone for design reasons. Until recently, bioconductor.org was generated and served by a single server (master.bioconductor.org). We are moving off that server to a more performant and cloud-based infrastructure; the change was necessitated by increasing and abrupt unsustainable traffic to the old infrastructure. Since late September, the site has been served from on entirely new infrastructure and rebuilt from the same package metadata (with the caveat that we are also in parallel integrating r-universe).

In the move to new infrastructure, the intent was to keep the package pages as close as possible to the originals. The new website html generation process also required update, so while the website looks very similar, it is built from scratch to be faster and more flexible. The first version changed more than it should have, and that's on me.

As of today, the pages are much closer to the old layout again:

- Same section order: Installation, Documentation, Details (with "See More"), Package Archives.
- "In Bioconductor since" uses the same source as before, so it agrees with the badge again (limma: BioC 1.6 or earlier, > 21.5 years).
- The duplicate download-rank row is gone.
- The Documentation links that led back to the same page are fixed. That was a bug in the tool that builds the pages, not intended behaviour.
- NEWS, the installation pointer and the unlinked base packages (splines ships with R) are as they were on the old pages.
- The code browser link returns once code.bioconductor.org's certificate problem is fixed. I have testing that runs each day that checks this.

Going forward, the package pages should stay close to what you were used to. The new website can generate PR review sites, so we can have live previews of substantial changes.

If you want the longer story, the plan and current status are at https://seandavi.github.io/bioc-infrastructure/ ("How bioconductor.org works" and the roadmap are the best starting points). If anything else is missing or wrong, reply here or file a report at https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues. I also have a talk that I gave to the Bioconductor Technical Advisory Board that might be of interest to a few folks here: https://talks.seandavis.net/2026-10-01-bioc-tab/

Thanks, again, Gordon for the close reading and for the questions. Please keep them coming.

Best,
Sean

We live at the start of the age of AI. On one hand, thousands of badly behaved bots trawl academic websites like bioconductor.org relentlessy, bringing them to a standstill for genuine human users. And learning to align, supervise, restrain and co-work with the AI agent is a skill in itself that takes considerable time and effort. Gordon

BTW, it would be interesting to know some background information on why the home pages are completely redone like this. They seemed ok as they were, so I assume that it must have something to do with rebuilding the backend. What's happening? It would be interesting to know what the plans are.

Regards
Gordon
